48474: Elly 2022 has 513 A+/AA PA, 28 HR and 158 K after a 76-EV FSL sample in 2021. No league meets the mature training fallback rule, so rate stays +.032 and PA 119 versus 427 actual. His subsequent -.748 MLB rate is a noisy first-season result, not a failure of the unfit minor coefficient. Corrected actual-input peers Mead, Luciano and Soderstrom arrive, Cartaya does not. No retrospective arrival filter; real level exposures differ and this is not a certified identical profile.
52233: Elly 2023 has 186 AAA PA with 12 HR/50 K, followed by 427 MLB PA with 13 HR/144 K. His 109 IL contacts average 93.37 mph with EV95 116.3. Coverage-only rate falls +.189 to -.611; measurements recover some of it to -.425, still worse before +1.886 future hitting. Latest EV95 contributes +.518 while mean EV contributes -.237. The negative coverage/translation terms and refitted core cannot be called a justified power penalty. Only two IL and one FSL refined training people support the profile. Corrected peers Alvarez and Matos have much smaller next-year workloads than Garcia; Diaz has none. This exposure rule is not a guarantee of identical talent.
52798: Caminero 2023 has 510 AA/A+ PA, 31 HR and 100 K, plus 36 MLB PA. None of his minor leagues is tracked. The combined MLB-only benchmark stays +.308 in both new arms, at 234 PA versus 177 actual and -.154 actual rate. The raw fitted output is not his routed forecast. Corrected peers Luciano, Carter and Crow-Armstrong appear next year, Lawlar does not. Untracked is not poor contact talent; the peer paths emphasize opportunity variation.
56439: Caminero 2024 has 236 AAA PA, 13 HR/50 K and 177 MLB PA, 6 HR/38 K. His 167 IL readings average 93.27 mph, EV95 111.55 and best-half 104.72. Forecast drops +.588 to +.094 before +2.175 in 653 PA. Coverage accounts for much of the reduction, while the latest mean-EV term is -.522 and EV95 +.189. Those conditional correlated coefficients are not proof harder contact hurts. Corrected exposure peers Wood and Martinez receive substantial next-year PA, Hernaiz fewer, Ramos only twelve. Seventeen refined people is sparse support, not validation. This is a substantial false-low mechanism to repair.
53164: Langford 2023 has 200 professional PA, 10 HR/34 K/36 UBB, with just 26 AAA PA and 13 EV readings. Best-half EV 101.94 contributes +.105. Measurement rate +1.355 is closer than combined +1.439 to +.549, but worse than coverage-only +1.178. Fixed 215 PA versus 557 actual dominates the delivered-value shortfall. The profile has zero refined active training people. Corrected draft/rank peers Crews, DeLauter, Teel and Shaw have no AAA history at the origin; only Crews reaches MLB next year. They are recent draftees, not fabricated full-season AAA comparables.
57052: Kurtz 2024 has only 50 A/AA PA, 4 HR/10 K/12 UBB and no tracking. Exact fallback keeps the already useful prospect alternative +1.024, rather than reverting to original -.063. It still misses +5.150 in 489 PA and predicts only ten PA. Cam Smith's arrival alongside other draft peers' non-arrivals exposes opportunity heterogeneity. The minor tracking addition cannot solve a player with no measured contacts.
57610: Eldridge 2024 has 519 PA across four levels, 23 HR/132 K/56 UBB, but just 35 AAA PA and 20 measured contacts. Best-half 101.36 and hard-air .4 do not supply a full season of precise tracking. Rate falls +.468 to +.031; latest hard-air signed term is -.252, a conditional correlated effect rather than a physical claim power is bad. It is closer to the -3.373 result over just 37 MLB PA, but that small result cannot settle talent or trade value. Refined support is absent; the exposure/pedigree peers are diagnostic, not perfect AAA equivalents.
58477: Caceres 2024 has 167 DSL PA, zero HR, 18 K and 17 UBB at age 16. There is no tracking, so both arms preserve the prospect benchmark -.142 exactly. The original +.499 is a separate earlier model. Zero next-year PA supplies no observed rate, and neither the lower routed rate nor zero contribution validates eventual talent. All original-age DSL peers fail to arrive immediately as expected for this horizon.
51010: Crook 2023 has 325 AAA PA, 10 HR/117 K/40 UBB and 157 EV readings; his 2022 IL contact measurements remain unknown. Mean EV 87.36 and EV95 107.14 lift the new head relative to its coverage control (-.762 to -.617), but both are below the -.322 combined benchmark. Fixed eight expected PA versus zero actual yields only a small contribution reduction. No observed future rate exists. Actual AAA peers include both an arrival and several non-arrivals.
51766: Hicklen 2023 has 286 AAA PA with 10 HR/70 K/35 UBB after a 559-PA, 28-HR/202-K season. Only 2023 has known EV: 172 readings, best-half 101.20. Forecast falls -.536 to -1.419, mostly already present in the -1.344 coverage control. Latest mean EV contributes -.159. Five actual MLB PA at -15.356 rate are not a precise talent observation. One refined training person and high strikeouts make the inference uncertain; retain the small outcome rather than implying it confirms a huge skill decline.
51800: Herron 2023 has 539 AAA PA, 19 HR/103 K/68 UBB and 467 measured contacts across two years. Latest best-half falls 98.23 to 96.43 and EV95 104.65 to 102.08. Rate -.324 to -.560 reduces contribution .098 to .083 before zero PA. Yet the current hard-air term is positive for below-reference hard-air because its coefficient is negative; the direction is not a clean power explanation. Seven refined training people and unsuccessful AAA peers remain. No future rate is observed.
51352: Bichette 2023 has 1,988 MLB PA across three seasons versus only six AAA PA/contacts. New rate +.122 versus combined +1.449 appears successful before -2.243 future hitting, but latest minor mean EV contributes -.382 and angle dispersion -.308 from six contacts. Minor coverage already cuts to +.807. This tiny sample disproportionately moves a mature hitter, a clear reliability concern. Later outcomes do not make that mechanism sensible.
55353: Bichette 2024 has 1,634 recent MLB PA versus 20 AAA PA and 18 measured contacts over two years. New rate -1.105 versus combined -.019 greatly worsens the miss before +2.424 in 628 PA. Latest angle SD 9.64 is -7.35 reference SDs and contributes -.567; prior six-ball angle SD adds -.429, and latest mean EV -.470. Twenty-four refined people does not certify this extreme short-sample shape. This is the opposite outcome of the apparent prior-year win and establishes why neither anecdote supports adoption.
55521: Alvarez 2024 has 635 MLB PA, 35 HR/95 K/53 UBB, with only eight minor contacts from a prior eleven-PA stint. The mature MLB production dominates the linear sum (+1.368 pooled quality). Rate +4.030 to +4.078 is a small talent change, while PA 547 versus 199 and +.920 actual hitting create the false high. This is not a large new minor-data effect or evidence he should have been forecast as a poor hitter. Exposure-based peers are not certified elite-talent matches.
55587: Perdomo 2024 has 388 MLB PA, 3 HR/58 K/36 UBB and 27 minor PA, with fourteen measured AAA contacts. Rate -.933 to -.681 improves slightly but misses +2.728 in 720 PA, versus expected 473. Below-reference hard-air produces a +.184 signed term because the fitted coefficient is negative. A lucky directional improvement is not a physical explanation of the breakout. Six refined people and varied peer careers leave substantial talent/opportunity uncertainty.
52468: Massey 2023 has 461 MLB PA, 15 HR/99 K/24 UBB and eight measured AAA contacts in twelve PA. Rate returns from coverage-only -.993 to -.327, essentially the combined -.329, before +.231 observed. The .961 predicted contribution nearly equals .959 actual, but expected 377 PA exceeds 356 and rate/environment errors offset. Eight contacts' mean angle 39.625 is +5.67 reference SDs and contributes +.281; the perfect-looking value is not validation of sample reliability. Peers show both useful players and failures.
